transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. At 12 years old, 'rough rattly growl' usually points to either a severe internal blockage choking the motor or worn motor bearings. We need to rule out a physical obstruction first. Please detach the hose and wand and look through them (or shine a torch down) to check for any blockages that might be causing that noise and suction loss.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
I've unplugged it and looked through the hose and wand. I dropped a coin through the hose and it went straight through, so there doesn't seem to be a blockage. What should I try next?

Since the hose was clear, the 'rattly growl' combined with weak suction on a 12-year-old machine suggests worn motor bearings or an internal blockage further down the airway. Please unplug it again and remove the main body from the base to check for large obstructions in the inlet or to see if the fan spins freely without grinding. If the fan wobbles or feels gritty, the bearings are likely shot.

I'm not very confident taking it apart, I only have a screwdriver and I've never opened it before. I should also say that after about five minutes of running there's a hot, burning electrical smell, and I once saw sparks flickering through the grille on top when I looked in a dim hall. Is that important?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, that is extremely important. A burning electrical smell and visible sparks are serious safety hazards indicating a failing motor, worn carbon brushes, or damaged internal wiring. Because you are not confident opening the unit and these faults involve live electrical components inside the casing, this must not be used again until it has been inspected by a qualified engineer. Given the age of the vacuum (12 years) and the severity of these symptoms, attempting to repair it yourself is unsafe; please arrange for an engineer to assess whether a motor replacement is viable or if the unit should be replaced.
